summary: feat(concur): add `expenses itemizations` and `reports exceptions` read commands
reason: There was no CLI surface to see how an itemization-required expense (for example a hotel folio) is split, or what blocks a report from being submitted. `expenses list` and `expenses get` expose the itemization sub-resource only as a link, and the per-expense hasExceptions / hasBlockingExceptions flags can read false while blocking exceptions exist (observed live: every itemization line reported no exceptions while the report carried several blocking ones). The only path was a hand-rolled authenticated GET against .../expenses/{id}/itemizations and .../reports/{id}/exceptions, both of which return bare JSON arrays and were confirmed live.
validated_outcome: go build, go vet and go test ./... pass; mocked-HTTP tests assert the exact request paths, bare-array pass-through, required flags/args and --context-type validation. Live-verified against a real report on a real tenant: `expenses itemizations` returned the expense's lines (amounts summing to the parent amount) and `reports exceptions` returned the exception list (empty when none), both inside the standard {meta,results} provenance envelope.
